case_title: State of M.P. v. Madan Lal
statutory_provisions: IPC s.376(2)(f) r/w s.511 (charged); IPC s.354 (substituted by High Court)
evidence_type: Victim testimony; mother's testimony; medical evidence; forensic examination of seized clothes; documents
aggravating_circumstances: Victim a seven-year-old girl (alleged offence against a minor)
mitigating_circumstances: None noted by the Supreme Court; the compromise relied on by the High Court was held not a valid ground
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.376(2)(f) r/w s.511 IPC; sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for five years
high_court_outcome: Conviction under s.376(2)(f) r/w s.511 set aside; convicted under s.354 IPC; sentence reduced to period already undergone (slightly more than one year)
neutral_facts: On 27 December 2008, the victim, aged about seven, was walking from her home toward Haar. The accused met her on the way and told her that her mother had gone toward the river. He took her near the river Parvati, removed her undergarment and made her sit on his lap. The victim shouted. The prosecution alleged that he then discharged on her private parts and on her stomach and washed the same. Hearing her cry, the victim's mother reached the spot, and the accused fled. The victim narrated the incident to her mother, who lodged a First Information Report. The investigating agency examined a number of witnesses, seized the accused's clothes, and sent certain articles to the forensic laboratory. After completing the examination, the investigators filed a chargesheet. The prosecution examined the victim, the victim's mother, two doctors, a head constable and an assistant sub-inspector, and exhibited nine documents. The defence led no evidence.
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted or assessed by the Supreme Court; the matter was remitted for reappraisal of the evidence
witness_credibility: Not assessed by the Supreme Court; the trial court had found the evidence credible
post_offence_conduct: Fled the spot when the victim's mother arrived
custody_duration: More than one year in custody (as noted by the High Court); the respondent was in custody at the time of the trial judgment
trial_duration: offence: 27.12.2008; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 01.02.2010; Supreme Court: 01.07.2015
legal_representation: For the State (appellant): G.D. Singh, Apoorv Kurup, Shreya Dubey. For the respondent: Asha Jain Madan, counsel engaged by the Court as the respondent did not appear
investigation_status: FIR lodged; investigation completed; chargesheet filed; case committed to Sessions Court; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: High Court did not refer to the trial evidence and was influenced by a compromise in a non-compoundable offence
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.376(2)(f) r/w s.511, five years RI. High Court: conviction altered to s.354, sentence reduced to period undergone. Supreme Court: High Court judgment set aside and remitted for fresh decision
prosecution_argument: The High Court did not apply appellate jurisdiction, dislodged the conviction in a laconic manner and failed to reappreciate the evidence; the sentence imposed was also criticised
defence_argument: Since the ingredients of s.376(2)(f) were not established, the conversion to s.354 was defensible and the sentence was not perverse
legal_principle_applied: Appellate court must reappraise the entire evidence and give reasons; compromise is impermissible in rape or attempted rape cases, which are non-compoundable
precedent_relied_upon: Amar Singh v. Balwinder Singh (2003) 2 SCC 518; State of M.P. v. Bhura Kunjda (2009) 17 SCC 346; K. Anbazhagan v. State of Karnataka (Criminal Appeal No. 637 of 2015); Shimbhu v. State of Haryana (2014) 13 SCC 318; Shyam Narain v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2013) 7 SCC 77; Baldev Singh and Ravindra confined to their facts
other_sentence_order: Respondent to be taken into custody forthwith; High Court to hear the appeal afresh; copy of judgment to be sent to the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, Bench at Gwalior
